title: stochastic eddy mapping - profiling scratch
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory notebook for a new way to decompose bursty ingress into small, overlapping 'eddies' (stochastic sub-bursts) to see how our batching + KV cache + prefill heuristics behave. Not a finished paper — personal notes while iterating on harness and measurement slices.

Hypothesis: 
- Breaking large spikes into many small, temporally-overlapped eddies reduces peak queue depth and reduces tail p99 compared to monolithic bursts, if the runtime can opportunistically merge and prefill.
- However, if eddies are too short (<= 20 ms inter-arrival), kernel wakeups and context-switch noise dominate and tail gets worse. There's a sweet spot around 50-120 ms window for our GPU kernels.

Test harness (local mini-fleet):
- 4 x A100-sim (profile mode) nodes, single model variant: small-llama-13B-8bit
- Runtime flags: --continuous-batching=true --batch-window-ms=30/60/120 (sweep) --kv-cache-ttl=15m --prefill-enabled=true --prefill-horizon=8
- Ingress generator: stochastic-eddy-arrivals v0.3 (see gen params below)
- Measurement: client p50/p90/p95/p99 latency from request submit -> first-token + tokens/sec; server queue depth histogram (1s buckets), batch size distribution sampled at 10k events.

Eddy generator params (JSON-like for reference):
- mean_eddy_size: 12 requests (Poisson)
- eddy_duration_ms: 40-400ms (uniform sweep)
- eddy_overlap_pct: 20/50/80% (controls how much new eddies start before prior finish)
- base_ramp: background poisson 2 qps
- spike_count: 30 spikes over 10m test window
- note: each request payload 120 tokens (prompt) + 20 tokens expected generation.

Run notes (quick logs):
- run-2025-02-09-13: batch-window 30ms, eddy_duration 100ms, overlap 50%
  - p50: 42ms, p90: 98ms, p95: 165ms, p99: 412ms
  - mean batch size: 6.1, batch size stdev: 2.9
  - queue depth peak: 31, avg: 3.8
  - observations: prefill hit rate ~73% (prefill horizon 8); many small batches — kernel overhead visible in p95/p99.

- run-2025-02-09-14: batch-window 60ms, eddy_duration 100ms, overlap 50%
  - p50: 38ms, p90: 86ms, p95: 140ms, p99: 290ms
  - mean batch size: 9.7, batch stdev: 3.4
  - queue depth peak: 26, avg: 5.1
  - observations: slightly lower tail and fewer tiny batches. Prefill hit rate ~78%.

- run-2025-02-10-09: batch-window 120ms, eddy_duration 100ms, overlap 50%
  - p50: 45ms, p90: 95ms, p95: 155ms, p99: 360ms
  - mean batch size: 12.8, batch stdev: 4.6
  - queue depth peak: 44, avg: 8.2
  - observations: larger batches but higher overall queue depth (saw some queueing backlog). p99 slightly worse than 60ms case.

- run-2025-02-11-11: batch-window 60ms, eddy_duration 30ms (tight eddies), overlap 80%
  - p50: 48ms, p90: 110ms, p95: 210ms, p99: 630ms
  - mean batch size: 4.3, stdev: 2.2
  - notes: kernel wake/teardown overhead dominates; prefill falling to ~52% due to short eddy horizon. Not good.

Micro-inspection: batch size vs latency scatter (sampled rows) — ascii-ish:
- batch_size | median_latency_first_token
- 1 | 26ms
- 2 | 34ms
- 4 | 58ms
- 8 | 92ms
- 12 | 140ms
- 16+ | 210ms
Interpretation: throughput wins with larger batches but diminishing returns; small variance for 2-8 cluster, then tail increases more sharply past ~12 due to kv cache churn and token-step kernel effects.

Prefill breakdown (60ms/100ms eddy):
- prefill satisfied requests: 78%
- partial-prefill (some context in cache but not full): 12%
- no-prefill: 10%
Notes: partial-prefill correlates with p95 spike clusters. We should instrument prefills-per-token and which keys miss.

Errors & anomalies observed:
- two 500s during long-run (2025-02-09-14 window) when node transient GC spike coincided with large batch creation. Need better SRE tracing (trace ids: sample TRC# 20250209-1418-31).
- batch-slicing edge case: when batch-window increases >100ms and eddy overlap high, we saw head-of-line blocking where small urgent requests stuck behind large multi-second batches. Possibly need priority lanes or preemption.

Quick conclusions so far:
- Sweet spot for these eddy parameters on our config: batch-window ~60ms, eddy_duration ~80-140ms, overlap ~40-60% gives good tradeoff between lower p99 and reasonable queue depth.
- Too-small eddies (<=40ms) cause kernel wake overhead and prefill misses — avoid.
- Too-large batch-window (>100ms) reduces tail for bulk but increases queue depth and head-of-line blocking risk. Consider preemptive slice or fast-path lane for small requests.

Action items / next experiments:
- (A) Add a preemptive fast-lane that interrupts batch assembly if a request has latency-sensitive flag. Quick prototype: if request.headers.X-urgent=true, bypass batching or cap batch-window to 10ms. Test impact on throughput and tail.
- (B) Instrument per-request prefills: log key count hits/misses and horizon-lag to trace p95 spikes to concrete cache misses.
- (C) Sweep eddy_overlap from 10% to 90% with batch-window fixed 60ms to map collision regime.
- (D) Repeat suite with quantized 4-bit variant to see kernel wake characteristics (might change optimal window).
- (E) Run on real Dedicated small fleet (2x real A100) for 1-hour soak to check for rare tails and GPU warmup drift.

Notes to self / heuristics draft:
- heuristic: prefer many small overlapping eddies when background load > 5 qps and model supports prefill horizon >= 6 tokens.
- heuristic: increase batch-window by +10ms when prefill hit rate above 85% and avg batch size < 8 to trade a little latency for better token-efficiency.

Open questions:
- How much of p99 is attributable to kernel wake vs KV-cache eviction vs network jitter? Need to break down server-side traces into those buckets.
- Is there a cheap approximation to detect when an eddy will produce only tiny batches so we can accelerate it? e.g., arrival curve predictor using last-200ms slope.

Random scratch formulas/logs:
- arrival_slope = (requests_last_200ms - requests_prev_200ms) / 200ms  // crude
- if arrival_slope > 0.02 req/ms then tag eddy as "rising" and keep prefill-horizon=12 else prefill-horizon=6

Useful links / reference commands used:
- generator repo: github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-sims/tree/eddymode (local branch: eddy-sweep)
- perf tool: ./bin/collect-traces --sample 1/200 --backoff 3s
- quick plotting script: scripts/plot-eddy-results.py (saves to /tmp/eddy-plot-<ts>.png)

Timestamped log snippet (raw client lines):
[2025-02-09 13:12:03.233] reqid=9c1a submit -> first=36ms tokens=28
[2025-02-09 13:12:03.276] reqid=9c1b submit -> first=124ms tokens=28
[2025-02-09 13:12:03.312] reqid=9c1c submit -> first=42ms tokens=28
[2025-02-09 14:18:31.902] ERROR node-2:500 GC-surge -> request batched size 18 dropped 2 reqs -> 500

Closing notes:
This is a living scratchpad. The initial numbers look promising for a mid-range batch-window (60ms) for eddy-mode traffic. Main next steps: implement preemptive fast-lane prototype and run dedicated soak. Share short summary with Lina and SRE to prioritize trace instrumentation.

-- Marcus
